newsitem.title: USA: US Coast Guard closes part of upper Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: US Coast Guard closes part of upper Mississippi.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard closed navigation Thursday on the upper Mississippi River from Minneapolis, Minn., to Guttenberg, Iowa.

High waters and potential flooding prompted the Coast Guard to impose a "safety zone" on that stretch of the river, said Bob Hildebrand, chief warrant officer at the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in in St Louis.
"We could expand the safety zone and follow the water downward," Hildebrand said.
The water was so high that it was spilling over the gates of many locks, he said.
"Barge traffic was closed to all except for vessels working directly with the official flood response efforts," Hildebrand said.

"There is not much activity up there at the moment. We decided April 9 to put a safety zone into effect and it was imposed on Thursday," he added. The zone extends from River Mile 857.6 at Minneapolis to Mile 615.1 at Guttenberg.
"We have a very fast running river and it is being monitored and evaulated every day as to when it can be reopened," he said.
